subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should this issue be fixed as one grouped Codex harness lifecycle repair, or split so mirrored-history parsing, shared-client cleanup, and fallback transcript continuity are owned separately?
rationale: The source paths are coupled in the reported failure, but the open partial PR and related issues show that each slice has different proof, compatibility, and replay-safety concerns.

options.title: Sponsor grouped harness fix
options.body: Treat this issue as the canonical grouped repair and require proof for mirror handling, shared-client lease safety, and fallback transcript continuity together.

options.title: Land warning fix only
options.body: Let the open partial PR reduce missing-file warning noise while keeping this issue open for the remaining runtime and failover behavior.

options.title: Split after live repro
options.body: Ask for a targeted active-memory/failover reproduction first, then split narrower follow-ups by root cause.

recommendation.title: Sponsor grouped harness fix
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the canonical grouped repair and require proof for mirror handling, shared-client lease safety, and fallback transcript continuity together.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest history owner for the mirrored-history reader and attempt-context integration surface.
